'''Werner Stumm''' (1924 – 14 April 1999) was a Swiss [[chemist]]. After earning his doctorate in [[inorganic chemistry]] at the University of [[Zürich]] in 1952 (with a dissertation titled ''Versuche zur analytischen Anwendung von Austauschcharzen''<ref>{{cite thesis|last=Stumm|first=Werner|title=Versuche zur analytischen Anwendung von Austauschcharzen|year=1952|url=https://archive.org/details/IA41507222_0032|type=Doctoral thesis|publisher=University of Zürich}}</ref>), he moved to the U.S., where he was active as a [[professor]] at [[Harvard University]] until 1969. From 1970 until 1992, he was head of the Swiss Federal Water Resources Centre [[EAWAG]].<ref name="Obituary_NAP">{{cite book | title=Memorial Tributes | publisher=National Academies Press | publication-place=Washington, D.C. | date=2002-06-11 | isbn=978-0-309-08457-4 | doi=10.17226/10403 | page=}}</ref>

Werner Stumm was an active researcher in several aspects of [[geochemistry]]. During the early part of his career, he was influenced by the ideas of [[Lars Gunnar Sillén]] and [[Robert Garrels]] regarding aqueous chemical equilibria. He developed models where the ideas by Sillén regarding [[chemical equilibrium|equilibria]] were combined with improved descriptions of [[kinetics (chemistry)|kinetically controlled]] reactions (i.e. slow reactions that do not reach equilibrium, e.g. [[weathering]]). He, in particular, made contributions to the knowledge of the reactions at the [[interface (chemistry)|interface]] of [[mineral]]s and water. In his more than 200 scientific articles, he showed, among other things, that the rate by which a [[mineral]] weathers depends on the surface [[charge (chemistry)|charge]], which in turn is controlled by factors such as [[pH]] and the chemical composition of aqueous solutions.

Stumm is also known for writing the influential book ''Aquatic Chemistry'', together with James J. Morgan, and several other books on the interplay between [[mineral]] surfaces and water.

The [[European Association of Geochemistry]] quinquennially awards a [[Science Innovation Award]] medal named in his honour for work in low-temperature and surface geochemistry.

== Prizes and awards ==
* [[Albert Einstein World Award of Science]] from the [[World Cultural Council]] (1985)<ref>{{cite web|title=Albert Einstein World Award of Science 1985|url=http://www.consejoculturalmundial.org/winners-science-wernerstumm.php|accessdate=August 13, 2013|archive-date=June 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140606235321/http://www.consejoculturalmundial.org/winners-science-wernerstumm.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* [[Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement]] (1986)
* ''Teknologie [[honorary degree|hedersdoktor]] (doctor honoris causa) [[Royal Institute of Technology]] (Sweden) (1987)''.<ref>[http://www.kth.se/om/fame/hedersdoktorer/1.3974 KTH: Hedersdoktorer 1944-2008] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100324033630/http://www.kth.se/om/fame/hedersdoktorer/1.3974 |date=2010-03-24 }}, accessed 13 April 2009</ref>
* [[Marcel Benoist Prize]] (1990)
* ''[[V. M. Goldschmidt Award]]'' (1998)
* ''[[Stockholm Water Prize]]'' (1999)
